attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded to white on a background of var(--surface). In the default light theme --surface is #ffffff, so the "Embargo until" label is invisible and only the amber outline renders. The dark theme is unaffected, so this breaks the default theme specifically. This fails WCAG 1.4.3.

The unpublish control is a non-focusable span with only a mouse onClick. It has no button role, no tabIndex, and no Enter/Space handler, so keyboard-only editors cannot reach or activate it. This fails WCAG 2.1.1, and the PR states these editors use the queue.

The unpublish control has no accessible name. Its only content is an icon marked aria-hidden, so screen readers announce nothing meaningful and the control has no role or state. This fails WCAG 4.1.2.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: aria-label or visible text on the unpublish span; `<TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" />` is the sole content

attacks.claim: The unpublish control has no focus-visible style. Its only visual state is hover, so keyboard focus would give no visible cue even if the control became focusable. This is a WCAG 2.4.7 gap that is secondary to the operability problem above.
attacks.evidence: `.unpublish:hover { color: var(--danger); background: var(--surface-hover); }` with no `:focus-visible` rule

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish has no try/catch, no error message, and no busy or disabled state. A rejected onUnpublish is unhandled and the editor gets no feedback, so the row can keep showing a stale 'published' status. A second click during the in-flight call can open another confirm and fire a duplicate unpublish against the same story.
attacks.evidence: `if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);` with no try/catch, no pending state, and no disabled state on the trash control

attacks.claim: The PR puts a one-click unpublish control on every queue row, and the diff contains no role or permission check. The server endpoint behind onUnpublish is not in the diff, so the artifact does not show that unpublish is restricted to authorized roles. This must be confirmed before merge.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any role or permission check for unpublish. Code shows only `const ok = await confirm({...}); if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);`

attacks.claim: Unpublishing a live, publicly visible story is destructive, and early-release embargo breaches may need to be traced. The diff adds no audit event, log, or metric for the unpublish action, so there is no record of who unpublished what or any alert on spikes or failures.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: audit logging, telemetry, or event emission in DraftRow.tsx or in the onUnpublish wiring; the diff only adds the confirm call and the await.

attacks.claim: The embargo label shows a clock time in the newsroom timezone with no zone label and no year. Screen reader users and editors outside that zone may misread the lift time.

The embargoed flag is computed once per render from the client clock and is never re-evaluated. A row can show an embargo that has already lifted, or miss one that has started, until the next render or data refresh. A malformed embargoUntil makes the badge silently disappear, since the NaN comparison is false.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: The confirm body says the story 'will be removed from the site,' but the diff does not mention cache purge, syndication retraction, or partner notification. This may be a scope gap, not a defect in the code shown, but the PR should state what it does and does not retract.
attacks.evidence: body: `"${draft.headline}" will be removed from the site and returned to drafts.` ABSENT: cache invalidation, syndication retraction, or partner notification.

attacks.claim: The diff adds new behavior (embargo derivation, status-gated unpublish, timezone formatting, confirm-then-call flow) with no tests.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any test file or test change in the diff.
